subject: system() does not seem to work within a shiny app... why is this?

messages.author: 39f5a1aeeec9eadd
messages.subject: system() does not seem to work within a shiny app... why is this?
parts:
ui.R

shinyUI(bootstrapPage(

  submitButton(),

  textInput('txt', 'text')
  
))


server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  systemCall <- reactive({

    input$txt

    system('ls > tmpFile.txt')
  
  })
  
})


... this is a simplified version of my problem. my full code, has the system() call inside a function that is called by a reactive function in shinyServer.

Why does this not work?

Thanks, in advanced

Dan

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: system() does not seem to work within a shiny app... why is this?
parts:
It's because reactive expressions are lazily evaluated; since systemCall is never used by anyone, its code is never executed.

You can create an observer to get the code to execute:

observe({ systemCall() })

Or just replace systemCall altogether with:

observe({

You can read more about reactive expressions (aka conductors) and observers (aka endpoints) in the "Reactivity Overview" chapter of the tutorial:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview

messages.author: ec79ef2df02af517
messages.subject: Re: system() does not seem to work within a shiny app... why is this?
parts:
Maybe output the value of the system() call from within shinyServer() to an Rds file. Then load the Rds file from a separate R script, but include the R script as a source in server.R

Without actually writing the code.....

1. Output value of system() call, found within shinyServer(), to an Rds file.
2. R script called system.R loads the Rds file and saves the value to a variable.
3. In server.R "source" system.R, but outside of shinyServer() function:

source("system.R", local=TRUE)

This should execute the code found in system.R, and make the variable containing Rds/system() data available.

If feels a bit clunky, but I think it should work.
